01

The research question

Where does reversal end — and momentum begin?

The same cross-section behaves differently at different clocks. The project maps that boundary before committing capital to either story.

Source · Research notebook, Modules 2–3
4-HOUR HORIZON

Mean reversion

Panic selling and forced liquidations push prices below fair value. The snap-back can be tradable.

4–8h

Reversal dominates the shortest lookbacks.

21-DAY HORIZON

Momentum

Persistent institutional reallocation keeps relative winners winning across a longer horizon.

21d

Trend survives when the latest noisy bar is skipped.

Dollar-neutralLong dollars equal short dollars.
Gross leverage 1.050% long and 50% short exposure.
No look-ahead biasDecisions at bar t earn only bar t+1.

04

The discovery

The signal changes sign with the clock

The empirical horizon scan exposes a structural transition: immediate cross-sectional returns reverse; medium-horizon returns persist.

Source · Research notebook, Module 3

Empirical horizon scan

Raw momentumLagged momentum
At 4 hours, “momentum” has a Sharpe of −3.80. That isn't momentum — it's a rubber band.

Skip one four-hour bar and the real signal appears: the lagged series peaks at a Sharpe of 1.63 at 72 hours.

05

Alpha 1

Fade the liquidation cascade

A six-day, 36-bar volume Z-score amplifies short-horizon reversal bets during abnormal-volume shocks.

Source · Research notebook, Modules 4 & 6
3.80Pure gross Sharpe
3.80Volume-cond. Sharpe
0.20Annualized vol

When a coin crashes on abnormal volume, the model treats forced margin selling as a temporary dislocation — and fades the panic.

The honest result

Gross Sharpe 3.80. Net Sharpe after 7 bps costs: −1.12. A beautiful signal that cannot be traded.

06

Alpha 2

Let medium-horizon winners keep running

A 21-day cross-sectional momentum signal, delayed by one bar and rebalanced daily instead of every four hours.

Source · Research notebook, Modules 5 & 6
21%Gross return

Two deliberate choices

01 Skip the latest four-hour bar to remove immediate microstructure bounce.

02 Rebalance every 24 hours — six bars — to control fee drag.

The executable alpha

After 7 bps limit-order costs, the strategy keeps a Net Sharpe of 0.87 (1.03 In-Sample, 0.57 Out-of-Sample).

The blend

Diversification works — until the bill arrives

The two alphas correlate at ρ = −0.09. Gross mean–variance optimization loves that diversification (3.85 gross Sharpe). Net optimization refuses to pay for the turnover friction and allocates 100% to momentum.

10

Research perspective

Turning market structure into an executable strategy

A reflection on the research choices that transformed an observed pattern into a testable, cost-aware portfolio.

I built this statistical arbitrage system to understand where short-horizon reversal gives way to persistent momentum across liquid cryptocurrency markets. The research calibrated parameters strictly on In-Sample data (2022–2023) and verified persistence on an untouched 2024 Out-of-Sample test set. By standardizing to daily √252 annualization and pricing 7 bps realistic limit-order costs, momentum achieved a 1.03 In-Sample Net Sharpe and 0.57 Out-of-Sample Net Sharpe (0.87 Full Sample). A rigorous single-index OLS regression against BTCUSDT verified β = 0.001 (t = 0.11, R² = 0.00%) with an annualized alpha of +15.54% (t = 1.81, p = 0.071) — demonstrating genuine statistical edge from cross-sectional relative value.

— Ayan · Project reflection
01

Strict OOS Validation

Calibrated on 2022–2023; holds out-of-sample in 2024 with 0.57 Net Sharpe at standard daily √252 scaling.

02

Turnover kills alpha

The 4-hour reversal's 3.80 gross Sharpe collapses to −1.12 net under daily rebalancing. 21d momentum survives at 0.87 net.

03

Statistically Significant Alpha

Demeaned ranks produce β = 0.001 to Bitcoin, R² = 0.00%, and an annualized alpha of +15.54% (t = 1.81, p = 0.071).

Methodology

  • Dollar-neutral construction; ranks demeaned every bar
  • Gross leverage 1.0: 50% long / 50% short
  • No look-ahead bias: decisions at t earn t+1

Execution model

  • Daily momentum rebalance: every 24h / six bars
  • Limit-order cost model: 7 bps
  • Market-order stress case: 20 bps
